clue.text: Something to invest in a mine in California

indicators.note: 'a mine in California' places the words for a mine inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A tip for an investor: put your money into a Californian gold mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A PIT inside CAL, giving C-A PIT-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Money set aside for investment in a business is its funds or stock of wealth, the financial sense of the word.

clue.text: Blade to snub girl

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore or snub them pointedly
a lass is a girl, chiefly in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A swordsman's weapon used to rebuff a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, curved sword once used by sailors and pirates is a type of blade.

clue.text: Light meal for one having share

definitions.text: Light meal for one having share

parts.words: Light meal for one having share
parts.note: read as a simple lunch for one person to split with others, but 'share' is a ploughshare, the blade of a plough, so the one having it is a farmer who ploughs

explanation.surface: A small meal served to someone who is sharing it with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'share' looks like dividing food; it is the cutting blade of a plough. A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle is named after the farm labourer who drove a plough, the one with the share.

clue.text: Function with good taste

parts.note: tan is the short form of the tangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Something that works well and has refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' is a maths function here, the tangent, written TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, distinctive flavour is a strong taste.

clue.text: Some entwined in fat sailor's rope

indicators.note: the word for 'some' is wound into the middle of the word for fat, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
any means some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Some threads twisted into greasy fat to make a seaman's line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entwined in' puts ANY inside LARD: L-ANY-ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cord used on ships to secure rigging or hold something, now also one worn round the neck for a pass.

clue.text: Unusual feature of bee-eater heard in Arab city

indicators.note: the description is said out loud, and its sound gives the spelling of the city

parts.note: the word bee-eater has three E's in a row, an unusual feature of its spelling, a 'triple E'

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes a strange trait of a bee-eater in a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: The feature is in the spelling, not the bird: bee-eater contains EEE, a 'triple E', which said out loud is TRIPOLI, the capital of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Libya is a city in the Arabic-speaking world.

clue.text: City near the shambles

indicators.note: a shambles is a mess, so the letters of the words before it are in disarray

explanation.surface: A town close to the slaughterhouse or the scene of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the shambles' signals an anagram of NEAR THE, an older spelling of the Iranian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Iran, here in an older spelling, is a major city.

clue.text: Tick head off — it's dubious

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for tick is removed, taking its head off

parts.note: a tick, as in 'just a tick', is a moment, a jiffy

explanation.surface: Removing a tick's head is a doubtful procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' looks like the parasite or a check mark; it is a moment, JIFFY, and 'head off' drops the J.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something doubtful or uncertain is questionable.

clue.text: Teetering, hove home, half cut, being this?

definitions.text: Teetering, hove home, half cut, being this?

indicators.note: cut is used for drunk, and the drunken letters stagger into a new order
half of the word home is taken, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A drunk sways his way home, half-cut, and the clue asks what he is.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of TEETERING + HOVE + HO (half of 'home') makes the answer, and the whole clue pictures someone who has had a drink too many. 'Half cut' is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having drunk too much, describing the swaying reveller in the scene.

clue.text: Was inspiring well in Independent

indicators.note: the word for well sits inside the abbreviation for Independent

parts.note: IND is the standard abbreviation for Independent, as on a ballot
hale means healthy, well

explanation.surface: Someone motivating while fit, within the newspaper's pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' looks like motivating; here it means breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring in its literal sense is drawing breath into the lungs.

clue.text: God, northern, appearing live, is a nuisance

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
a performer appearing live is seen in person, there in body

explanation.surface: A Norse deity from the north makes a personal appearance and causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a persistent source of annoyance, like a splinter lodged under the skin.

clue.text: Ship with king in before now

indicators.note: the king's letter goes inside the word for before now

parts.note: ago means in the past, before now
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A ship carrying a monarch, from a past age.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Jason sailed this vessel in search of the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Hang about like a sailor apparently

definitions.meaning: a tar is a sailor, so read as tar plus -y the word seems to mean sailor-like, though it really means covered in tar

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is lingering or delaying; the other treats 'tar', slang for a seaman, as the root, so 'apparently' marks the false etymology.

clue.text: Satan heading off to produce this

definitions.text: Satan heading off to produce this

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for Satan is dropped, removing its head

parts.note: Satan is the Devil

explanation.surface: The Devil sets out to create wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the Devil without his D, and Satan going off to cause wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness is what Satan sets off to produce in the clue's picture.

clue.text: Aussie girl, one in Scottish inlet

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the Scottish word for a strait

parts.note: a kyle is a narrow strait or sound in Scotland, as in Kyle of Lochalsh
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Australian woman standing in a Scottish sea channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a typical Australian girl's name (Kylie Minogue).
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name strongly linked with Australia, borne by the singer Minogue.

clue.text: One tempting lord with a bit of nooky

parts.note: sire is a form of address for a lord or king

indicators.note: only a small piece of the word nooky is taken, its first letter

explanation.surface: A seductive nobleman offering a little sex.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth the Sirens lured sailors with their singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman, after the sea nymphs who lured sailors, is one who tempts.

clue.text: Dog to be broken in someday

indicators.note: the word someday is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A puppy that will be house-trained one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken in' looks like training a dog; 'broken' signals an anagram of SOMEDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A white Siberian breed of spitz is a type of dog.

clue.text: Conceal lord in a bulrush

annotationWithheld.why: 'Conceal lord in a bulrush' (7): NAILROD is an anagram of LORD IN A, but 'Conceal' does not signal an anagram and no hidden or container reading gives the answer; likely an OCR misread of the indicator, with no scan to confirm

clue.text: Vice-roy becoming obscure?

parts.note: a vice is a sin
roy is an old spelling of roi, French for king

explanation.surface: A colonial governor fading from public notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice-roy' looks like a governor; split it, vice is SIN and roy (from French roi) is KING. The question mark marks the figurative definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinking into oblivion means fading from notice, so a figure in decline is going under.

clue.text: Make up on a tart

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: slap is slang for theatrical make-up
per means for each or for a, as in 'ten pounds per head'

explanation.surface: Applying cosmetics to a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry; it is a derogatory British word for a promiscuous woman, and slapper is its slang equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang insults for a promiscuous woman.

clue.text: Nothing found in woods but rocks?

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is discovered inside the word for woods

parts.note: groves are small woods
O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: In the forest there is nothing but stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like stones; it is the verb, to dance or move to music, which grooves also means.
explanation.definitionFit: To move rhythmically to music, enjoying it, is to dance with the beat, the slang verb sense.

clue.text: New student is more audacious

definitions.meaning: cheekier, the comparative of fresh in its sense of impudent

explanation.definitionFit: A British first-year undergraduate, and the comparative of fresh meaning cheeky.

clue.text: One starting to experience difficulties

definitions.meaning: a person who sets up an institution or business
to fail or sink, like a ship filling with water

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who establishes an organisation, and a verb meaning to collapse or sink like a stricken ship.

clue.text: Costume worn by a singer

parts.note: robes are garments, a costume
clothes that are on are being worn

explanation.surface: An outfit worn by a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Robeson was an American bass singer and actor, famous for 'Ol' Man River'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson was a celebrated American bass vocalist.

clue.text: Fit wire requiring lead

indicators.note: the word for wire is lacking its leading letter, so it still needs it

parts.note: a cable is a wire

explanation.surface: An electrician installing a wire needs a flex to connect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like an electric flex; it is the leading letter, which CABLE is short of.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fit for a task means being competent or capable.

clue.text: Fusion reactor to corrode releasing tritium

indicators.note: the word for corrode lets go of the letter for tritium

parts.note: to rust is to corrode
T is the chemical symbol for tritium

explanation.surface: A nuclear reactor rusting away and leaking radioactive hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: A torus is a ring-doughnut shape, the shape of a tokamak fusion reactor such as JET.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped surface; a tokamak fusion reactor is built in this doughnut form.

clue.text: Sybil's heart given to her Basil perhaps

indicators.note: the central letter is handed over and added after her
the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the name Sybil, whose middle letter is taken

explanation.surface: Sybil Fawlty's affection belongs to her husband Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: Sybil and Basil are the hotel-keeping couple in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, but Basil here is the culinary plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an example of an aromatic plant used in cooking.

clue.text: Mountain in Vietnam

indicators.note: the mountain's name lies inside the word Vietnam

explanation.surface: A peak somewhere in South-East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The volcano is in Sicily, not Vietnam: 'in' simply signals the letters within the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily's active volcano is a famous mountain.

clue.text: Makes stuck up-just so

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to gum something is to make it stick

explanation.surface: Pride makes a person conceited, just like that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' looks like the definition (conceited); split it: 'Makes stuck' is GUMS and 'up' turns it. 'just so' is the old sense of the answer, neat and trim.
explanation.definitionFit: The older meaning of the word is neat, trim and spruce, everything in order.

clue.text: Advising amputee, injured, to get maximum compensation

indicators.note: the two words are damaged and their letters reshaped

explanation.surface: A lawyer advises someone who lost a limb in an accident to claim the most they can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' signals the anagram of ADVISING AMPUTEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Courts award extra, exemplary sums to punish a wrongdoer, going beyond ordinary compensation.

clue.text: Tries again to practise endlessly

indicators.note: the word for practise loses its last letter, so it has no end

parts.note: to rehearse is to practise a performance

explanation.surface: Someone attempting something again in order to practise without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' is the legal sense: a court hears a case again.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that hears a case a second time tries it again.

clue.text: Square leg is cool

parts.note: a square corner is a right angle
in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A cricket fielding position, square leg, is a fine place to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square leg' looks like the cricket fielding position; split, square is RIGHT and leg is ON, since cricket's leg side is the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of hearty approval, slang meaning excellent or fashionable.
